turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict each
candidate's birefringence at 1064 nm, then select the 5 candidates whose
birefringence is CLOSEST to 0.1.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I estimated the 1064 nm birefringence from symmetry, dimensionality, and polarizable structural motifs. I discounted cubic/pseudocubic 3D frameworks as too low, and very heavy/lone-pair or strongly layered Te/Tl/Nb sulfides as likely too high. The closest-to-0.1 region is most likely populated by moderately layered noncubic sulfide/selenide frameworks with anisotropic tetrahedral or chalcogenide layers.

Best candidates:

| Rank | candidate_id | Rationale | Estimated Δn |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 | c067 | Rb–Li–Zn sulfide, tetragonal/layered; strong c-axis anisotropy but sulfide polarizability keeps it moderate | ~0.100 |
| 2 | c048 | Hexagonal YCuSe₂-type layered selenide; Se/Cu layers give moderate-high optical anisotropy | ~0.098 |
| 3 | c041 | Na/Sr thioborate framework; anisotropic BS₃-type units but partially cross-oriented, near target | ~0.102 |
| 4 | c088 | YAgS₂ layered hexagonal sulfide; Ag–S polarizability and layered stacking give Δn near 0.1 | ~0.097 |
| 5 | c046 | K analogue of c067; similar layered Li–Zn–S motif, slightly less polarizable than Rb version | ~0.104 |

Final: c067, c048, c041, c088, c046
